implementation.receiver_model: struct TableWordPair: an 0x08-byte opaque byte run, alignas(4), with NO member names. The body writes two dwords at the object's displacements 0x00 and 0x04 and touches no other byte; the machine-derived receiver record is bounds_only with offsets [0, 4], distinct_offsets 2, max_offset 4, written_through 2, confidence INFERRED, and it says where the body reached, not what either word is. implementation.dispatch_model: none declared. abi_derived.dispatch records indirect_calls 0, call_offsets [] and vtable_shaped_loads 0, and the 12 instructions contain no register- or memory-operand transfer. The word the body WRITES at the receiver's +0x00 is a different thing from a word the body READS there, and only the former exists in this listing.
implementation.globals: two .rdata addresses, both WRITES: 0x013eb938 (0x010537bf) and 0x013ec458 (0x010537b8). Both are read out of the instructions' own little-endian immediates. receiver_evidence.record: abi_derived.receiver = {present true, register ECX, shape R-ALIAS, bounds_only true, offsets [0, 4], distinct_offsets 2, max_offset 4, written_through 2, confidence INFERRED}
receiver_evidence.what_the_listing_shows: 0x010537b6 MOV ESI,ECX, then 0x010537b8 MOV [ESI+0x4],imm and 0x010537bf MOV [ESI],imm. Two writes, no loads, no LEA, nothing at any other displacement, and ECX is dead from 0x010537b6 onward. The record's offsets were observed through the alias, which is why a scan of the listing for ECX's own operands finds no displacement at all -- a fact the FIELDS/OFFSETS check has to be told about and one the model states rather than hides.

branch.condition: bit 0 of the LOW BYTE of the entry stack word is CLEAR
branch.flags_provenance: Set by 0x010537b0 and read by 0x010537c5. Nothing between them touches the flags: 0x010537b5 PUSH, 0x010537b6 MOV reg,reg, and the two MOV-immediate stores all leave ZF untouched.

0x013eb938.written_by: 0x010537bf MOV dword ptr [ESI],0x13eb938 (bytes c7 06 38 b9 3e 01 -- no displacement byte, so the operand is bare [ESI])
0x013eb938.reading: A two-entry table whose two entries are the same import thunk. 0x011e06d0 is `FF 25 68 c4 3c 01  jmp DWORD PTR ds:0x13cc468`, and the PE import directory says the IAT slot 0x013cc468 is MSVCR90.dll!_purecall (hint 811). Ghidra's decompilation of this VA spells the same constant `&PTR_purecall_013eb938`, which is the same observation in different vocabulary.

0x013ec458.written_by: 0x010537b8 MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x4],0x13ec458 (bytes c7 46 04 58 c4 3e 01 -- one displacement byte, 0x04)
0x013ec458.reading: A table whose leading entry is 0x0055bf80, and 0x0055bf80 is a body of the SAME SHAPE as the one under reconstruction: mov [ebp-4],ecx / mov eax,[ebp-4] / mov [eax],0x13ec458 / mov ecx,[ebp+8] / and ecx,1 / je +0xc / push edx / call 0x00f47380 / ... / ret. Two independent bodies therefore install a table head at the object's displacement zero, which is what makes 'these two constants are table heads' a machine fact and not a naming decision.

data_constants.why_two_and_not_one: A third body fixes the shape. 0x01053790, sixteen bytes above this one, is the same eight-instruction destructor with a single store: test byte [esp+4],1 / push esi / mov esi,ecx / mov [esi],0x1403934 / je +9 / push esi / call 0x00f47380 / add esp,4 / mov eax,esi / pop esi / ret 0x4. The body under reconstruction is that shape with a SECOND such store, one instruction earlier, at +0x04. Three bodies, one shape, one of them with two words.
data_constants.what_is_NOT_claimed: That the two constants name a class, or that this body is the destructor of any particular type. See unresolved_questions.

sub_object_at_0x04.evidence: 0x01053780, immediately below this body, is 8 bytes: 83 e9 04 (sub ecx,0x4) followed by e9 28 00 00 00 (jmp 0x010537b0). It is the xref this target's own export records at 0x01053783, the immediate of that JMP.
sub_object_at_0x04.conclusion: A caller may legitimately hand this body a pointer four bytes above the object's real base, with the bias already applied. 0x010537b6 copies ECX into ESI unchanged and both stores go through ESI, so the body does NOT re-apply the -4. The model test drives exactly this case with a decoy word planted below the pointer it hands over.
sub_object_at_0x04.consequence_for_the_size: The receiver needs the two words the body rewrites and the sub-object at +0x04 that proves a second word exists, so it is modelled as 0x08 bytes.

the_one_callee.convention: cdecl, one dword argument: it loads [esp+0x4] into EAX, null-checks it (TEST EAX,EAX / JE +0xc), loads the .data word 0x016c8b44 into ECX, pushes the argument and calls 0x009276c0, then returns with a BARE C3 that leaves ESP alone. 0x010537cd ADD ESP,0x4 is therefore the caller's half of the cdecl pairing.
the_one_callee.what_this_body_uses_of_it: one dword argument, the object address, and no return value
the_one_callee.name: heap_release_00f47380. The name describes its own shape -- a guarded one-argument hand-off to a release function held in a global. That it is a particular named CRT entry point is an INFERENCE from the null check plus the shape, not something its bytes state, and it is labelled that way in the header.
the_one_callee.null_argument: The callee is null-safe, but this caller is not: 0x010537b8 dereferences the receiver unconditionally and faults first. The model test states this and deliberately does not drive it.

observed_mechanics_transcript: 0x010537b0 TEST byte ptr [ESP + 0x4],0x1 -- the first instruction, before the prologue push, so [ESP+0x4] is the entry stack word; operand width is BYTE, so only its low eight bits are tested.
0x010537b5 PUSH ESI / 0x010537d2 POP ESI -- the only saved register, balanced.
0x010537b6 MOV ESI,ECX -- the receiver alias. ECX is dead after this and the bias is not re-applied.
0x010537b8 MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x4],0x13ec458 -- the FIRST of the two stores, at displacement 0x04, immediate 0x013ec458 (bytes 58 c4 3e 01).
0x010537bf MOV dword ptr [ESI],0x13eb938 -- the SECOND store, at displacement 0x00, immediate 0x013eb938 (bytes 38 b9 3e 01).
0x010537c5 JZ 0x010537d0 -- the only branch; taken when bit 0 of the tested byte is clear; the target is inside the body.
0x010537c7 PUSH ESI / 0x010537c8 CALL 0x00f47380 / 0x010537cd ADD ESP,0x4 -- one cdecl call with the receiver as its single argument, cleaned up by the caller.
0x010537d0 MOV EAX,ESI -- the return value, the receiver, reached by both arms.
0x010537d3 RET 0x4 -- the callee owns the four-byte argument word.
Both stores precede the branch and precede the call, and both are unconditional: the object reaches the same state on both arms.

return_semantics.kind: a four-byte pointer to the receiver
return_semantics.machine_fact: 0x010537d0 MOV EAX,ESI is the only write to the return register and it is reached by falling out of BOTH arms -- it is the JZ target and it is the instruction after the release call. ESI was last written at 0x010537b6, from ECX, and is never written again. So every path returns the receiver, unchanged.
return_semantics.records_that_describe_it: abi_derived.return = {register EAX, register_class aggregate_unknown, void_possible false, confidence INFERRED} and abi.abi.return_semantics = 'unclassified_in_EAX'; ghidra_function.return_type = 'undefined', return_type_resolved false; Ghidra's decompilation types the function `undefined4 *` and returns param_1.
return_semantics.why_that_spelling: Width and value are machine-fixed; the C spelling is a source-side choice among the types of that width, and a pointer to the receiver is the one that is true of the value. The canonical ABI token is the prose 'unclassified_in_EAX', which no C declaration can spell, so the RETURN SEMANTICS check compares it as a string and lands on its 'differs or is semantically renamed' WARN. That WARN is about the vocabulary of the record, not about the reconstruction: the machine's own width state for this body is WIDTH_4_IN_EAX, provable from the complete listing, and the declared type is four bytes wide.
return_semantics.lifetime: The receiver is not freed by this body on the quiet arm, and on the releasing arm it is handed to 0x00f47380 with no further reference kept: the body returns the same address, so the CALLER, not this body, decides what a returned freed pointer means. The reconstruction does not claim anything about that and the test does not assert anything about it beyond the address value.

semantic_findings: The body is a two-word scalar-deleting-destructor shape: it rewrites the object's two leading words with a base pair of table heads, optionally releases the object, and returns the receiver.

The two immediates are table heads, read out of .rdata rather than assumed. 0x013eb938 is a two-entry table whose entries are both the MSVCR90.dll!_purecall import thunk at 0x011e06d0, which is why Ghidra names the location PTR_purecall_013eb938. 0x013ec458 is a table whose leading entry is 0x0055bf80, a body of this same shape.

Three independent bodies in the image (0x01053790, 0x010537b0, 0x0055bf80) install a table head at an object's displacement zero, so 'a destructor stores a table head into the object' is a pattern the image supports rather than an inference from one site.

The object has a second sub-object at +0x04: 0x01053780 is a thiscall adjustor (`sub ecx,4 / jmp 0x010537b0`) sitting eight bytes below this body, and it is this target's own recorded xref at 0x01053783. The body therefore receives an already-biased receiver and must not bias it again.
The flag argument's WIDTH is load-bearing, not its value: only bit 0 of the low byte is examined, so 0x00000100 does not release and 0xfffffffe does not release, while 0x00000101 and 0xffffffff do.

The single callee 0x00f47380 null-checks its argument, but this caller never benefits: both stores dereference the receiver with no test of any kind, so a null receiver faults at 0x010537b8 before the callee is reached.
The body's EAX return is the receiver on both arms, which is the pattern that lets a caller chain a further destruction step; that is an observation about the value, not a claim about any caller.

validation.compile_gate: clean build, zero warnings, zero errors, test exit 0, under g++ 16.2.1. The header additionally compiles clean as its own translation unit under the same flags (via a one-line TU that includes it), the .cpp compiles clean alone, and the whole pair builds and runs clean under clang++ -m32 with the same flags.
validation.optimization_gate: the pair was also built and run at -O1, -O2, -O3 and -Os: all five levels exit 0. Getting there required marking the test's trampoline wrapper noinline, for a reason the test file records at the wrapper: an inlined copy let the compiler fold the four argument pushes into the caller's own stack, and on the second trampoline entry the object pointer's slot came back holding the previous call's canary (0x5a5a5a5a) instead of the receiver, which faults inside the body.
validation.model_test: plain int main() with explicit checks, no framework and no external dependency. The one direct callee 0x00f47380 is defined in the test as an observer that records its argument, reads the object's two words AT THE MOMENT OF THE CALL, and can scribble over them so the reverse question (does anything re-write them after the call) is observable too. Ten cases: A branch polarity and the tested bit, ten rows; B exactly two words change, with four guard bytes below the object and two decoy words above, on both arms; C the stored words are never dereferenced; D the +0x04 sub-object receiver is not re-biased; E only the low byte of the stack word participates, eight rows driven through the trampoline because the declared parameter is a byte; F the release argument is the receiver and not a derivation of it (four checks; a fifth was written and then dropped as a duplicate of the first, since the address of the word at +0x00 is the object address itself); G store order relative to the call, from both sides; H the ABI measured in a trampoline (ESP balance, ESI restored, EAX holds the receiver, on both arms); I two calls, two objects, opposite flags; J the constants and displacements this package states. Byte-level assertion: no byte outside the object's first eight changed, guards included, on either arm, and all eight of them did.
validation.abi_measurement: ESP before the argument word is pushed and after the return, ESI loaded with a canary and read back, EAX read at the instruction boundary after the call, and ECX's effect confirmed by the object the body actually wrote. All four are samples, not conventions asserted in prose.

conditions: The original process is driven to an object whose +0x00 and +0x04 words hold a most-derived table pair, once with the deleting-destructor flag clear and once with it set.
A trace records the value in the entry stack word at 0x010537b0 and the ZF it produces, and which arm 0x010537c5 takes, confirming that the release is gated on bit 0 of that byte and on nothing else.
A trace captures the two words before and after 0x010537b8 and 0x010537bf, confirming the immediates 0x013eb938 and 0x013ec458 and the order the two stores happen in.

A trace captures the pointer 0x00f47380 receives, and separately the pointer the body returns in EAX, so the two are shown to be the same address and the caller-side consequence of a returned freed pointer can be settled.

A trace enters through the adjustor 0x01053780, so the -4 bias is observed arriving already applied and the absence of a second bias in this body is confirmed against a live call rather than against a model.

unresolved_questions: What class does this destructor belong to? No name is claimed and none is invented.
